answer: Each node commits an epoch-locked state root hashed with Blake3 over its dedicated 8 GB RAM array, seeded by a per-identity nonce certified in the prior epoch. First, registrant proves ownership by replaying that array under the trellis of parent hashes; verifier re-derives the root and rejects any duplicate. A crystal digest binds root to nonce, so copied state self-collides. The beacon epoch flag then confirms uniqueness network-wide. Duplicate root slashes the bond and evicts the seat. Covering 10,000 identities costs ~$4,200 in RAM-hours per epoch.
